stripText.remove: (Each diagram A, B, C, D shows two tubes meeting at a wall with a dotted normal line, and the angles i and r marked. In diagram A both i and r are measured between the tubes and the normal. In diagram B angle i is measured from the wall and r from the normal. In diagram C angle i is measured from the normal and r from the wall. In diagram D both i and r are measured from the wall.)

(Each diagram A, B, C, D shows an incident ray striking a surface and a reflected ray leaving it, with a dotted normal. In diagram A both the angle of incidence i and angle of reflection r are marked between the rays and the normal, on opposite sides, and are equal. In the other diagrams the angles are marked from the reflecting surface or on the wrong sides.)

(Each diagram i, ii, iii, iv shows a reflecting board with two tubes meeting at it and a vertical normal. In diagram (iv) the angle of incidence i is marked between the left tube and the normal and the angle of reflection r between the right tube and the normal, on opposite sides and equal. In (i) both angles are marked on the same side of the normal; in (ii) the angles are measured from the board surface; in (iii) the angles are marked incorrectly.)

(Diagram A shows a string with an upward pulse moving toward a rigid (fixed) wall. The options are four diagrams: (i) an inverted (downward) pulse located right next to the wall, moving away from it; (ii) an upright pulse next to the wall; (iii) an inverted pulse far from the wall, moving away; (iv) an upright pulse far from the wall.)
